pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — NewResourceServer now does DB init/ping plus a synchronous full search-index build inside the constructor, so a transient DB outage or slow/failed index build blocks or aborts whole-process/module startup instead of failing individual RPCs

pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:88 — With the global build lock gone, nothing limits concurrent Search requests for unindexed namespaces/resources, and each one fires its own full ListIterator rebuild (size 10, unbounded Limit), which lets a caller amplify load into DB and memory exhaustion

pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:216 — The new TotalDocs() log call reads b.cache without cacheMu right after starting the watch goroutine, which can write b.cache through getOrCreateIndex→BuildIndex, so a concurrent map read/write can crash the process fatally

pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:190 — Now that builds really run in parallel (no bleve lock), errgroup workers write the shared outer `err` (and totalBatchesIndexed++) without synchronization, so one worker's failed build can be overwritten to nil before `return err` and the failure is silently swallowed

pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:203 — The index is built from a ListIterator snapshot, but WatchWriteEvents subscribes only after group.Wait and starts from the latest RV (sql backend listLatestRVs), so writes committed between each namespace's snapshot and the subscription never reach the index; the reordered Init does not close this gap and the build RV is discarded

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:261 — When Init fails, the constructor returns nil without calling s.cancel(), so the context.Background search watch goroutine and the backend poller that search.init may already have started leak with no way to Stop them

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:321 — Stop() still sets s.initErr to "service is stopping/stopped" but no handler calls Init() anymore, so Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search keep executing against a stopped backend instead of failing fast.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:934 — IsHealthy no longer returns the Stop()-set initErr, so the server reports SERVING while shutting down or after Stop, which breaks health/readiness semantics during shutdown.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:216 — The new TotalDocs() call runs after the handleEvent goroutine starts, and bleve TotalDocs ranges b.cache with no lock, so an event that builds an index (map write at bleve.go:138) can race it and crash with a concurrent map iteration/write fatal error.

pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137 — Now that cacheMu is not held for the whole build, concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key (Search vs handleEvent getOrCreateIndex) both build and the last one to finish overwrites the cache, so watch-event writes that went into the earlier index can be silently dropped.

If the prior design relied on `Init()` to return an error when the server is stopping/stopped (e.g., via `initErr` being set during `Stop()`), that shutdown gating would no longer be enforced by RPC handlers. However, the diff does not show the `Stop()` implementation nor any `Init()` logic explicitly checking a “stopping” state, so the specific claim about `Stop` setting `initErr` and IsHealthy reporting `SERVING` during shutdown cannot be verified from the provided diff alone.

```go

if err != nil { ... return nil, err }

but on error it returns without any cleanup. However, the claim that `ctx` is `context.Background`-derived with no timeout/deadline is not verifiable from the provided diff (ctx creation isn’t shown), so that part can’t be confirmed as a concrete defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:949 — With Init() removed from the handlers, the initErr that Stop() sets ("service is stopping"/"stopped") is never checked again, so IsHealthy keeps reporting SERVING (the backend ping still works because backend.Stop only cancels) and CRUD/Search RPCs keep running during and after shutdown instead of failing fast

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `s.Init(ctx)` calls from multiple RPC handlers (e.g., `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/...`) and instead calls `s.Init(ctx)` once in `NewResourceServer`. However, the finding’s core claim—that `Stop()` sets `initErr` to a stopping/stopped sentinel and that `IsHealthy`/CRUD/Search should fail fast by re-checking `initErr` via `Init()`—cannot be verified from this diff because `Stop()` and any `initErr` semantics/health behavior are not shown here. From the shown code, `IsHealthy` simply delegates to `s.diagnostics.IsHealthy` and there is no visible check of `initErr` either before or after the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/server/module_server_test.go:36 — The storage-server integration test is now skipped for postgres in the same PR that moves blocking DB and index init into construction; the only coverage of the new startup path (InitializeModuleServer followed by a fixed 500ms sleep) is disabled, which can hide a real startup-time regression

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a Postgres skip in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` (`pkg/server/module_server_test.go`), so that integration coverage won’t run for Postgres in CI. In the same PR, `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` during construction and removes the per-RPC `Init` calls (e.g., `Create/Update/Delete/...` in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`), which is a meaningful startup-path change. Skipping the integration test for Postgres can therefore reduce coverage for the new “init at construction time” behavior on that DB. However, the claim that this is the *only* coverage of the new startup path (and the “fixed 500ms sleep”) is not verifiable from the provided diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:261 — When eager Init fails, NewResourceServer returns nil without calling s.cancel() or lifecycle.Stop(), so the already-initialized backend/DB and any search watch goroutine that started (context.Background at search.go:202) leak

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an eager `s.Init(ctx)` call inside `NewResourceServer` and returns `nil, err` on failure (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go). The diff does not show any corresponding cleanup/shutdown on that error path. Since `Init` can start long-lived work (e.g., `s.search.init(ctx)` launches a goroutine in search.go via `go func() { ... }()` and `Init` also starts the watcher), a failure partway through initialization could leave background activity/resources running even though the constructor returns an error. The finding’s specific mention of `s.cancel()`/`lifecycle.Stop()` isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the lack of any cleanup on constructor failure after starting background work is a real defect risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/server/module_server_test.go:36 — New postgres skip for the only storage-server-target integration test lands alongside eager Init (DB connect, full index build, pollers) in NewResourceServer, likely hiding a regression rather than a flaky environment.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a new skip for `dbType == "postgres"` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` (module_server_test.go), which reduces integration coverage on Postgres. In the same PR, `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` eagerly and fails construction on init errors, while per-RPC `Init` calls were removed (server.go). That combination can plausibly mask Postgres-specific init regressions in CI, but the claim that this is the “only storage-server-target integration test” and that it’s definitively hiding a regression is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — Eager Init in the constructor has no test for the failure path: on error the server returns nil without calling cancel(), and goroutines started by search.init or the backend poller leak with no Stop available.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds eager initialization in `NewResourceServer` (`err := s.Init(ctx)` and `return nil, err` on failure) and removes per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls. The PR does not add any test coverage for the new constructor failure path. The claim that `cancel()` is not called and that goroutines (e.g., ones started inside `search.init(ctx)` which now starts spans with the returned `ctx` and appears to spawn a goroutine) will leak is a plausible lifecycle concern, but it is not directly verifiable from the diff because the context/cancel ownership and any Stop/cleanup methods are not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:321 — Taking Init out of every RPC handler means Stop's "service is stopping/stopped" initErr no longer blocks requests, and no test covers how the server behaves after Stop.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `s.Init(ctx)` from all RPC handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.) and instead calls `s.Init(ctx)` once in `NewResourceServer` before returning the server. If runtime state changes after construction (e.g., `Stop` or other code mutating `s.initErr` / initialization state), those handlers no longer re-check init state on each request. The diff also doesn’t add any coverage around post-Stop behavior, so this lifecycle/behavior change isn’t exercised by tests in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137 — BuildIndex now builds without cacheMu, so concurrent builds for the same key (getOrCreateIndex check-then-build from Search and handleEvent) can run in parallel, and no concurrent-BuildIndex or -race test covers it.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire method (removed at lines ~85-88) but now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx` (added at ~137). This diff-grounded change allows concurrent callers to execute the expensive/index-creating portion (including `bleve.New(dir, ...)` for the same `key`/`dir`) in parallel before either caches the result, which can lead to duplicate builds and potential races/incorrect behavior when creating/opening the same on-disk index directory concurrently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:216 — New TotalDocs() call ranges over b.cache without holding cacheMu while the just-started handleEvent goroutine can write to the cache through BuildIndex, a data race no test exercises.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only adds a log line calling `s.search.TotalDocs()` in `searchSupport.init` and adjusts cache locking in `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` to lock only around `b.cache[key] = idx`. It does not show the implementation of `TotalDocs()` (or that it ranges over `b.cache` without `cacheMu`), so the claimed unsynchronized iteration/data race cannot be verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:304 — Init now runs the search index before initWatcher, and no test covers that order or the event gap between the index build and WatchWriteEvents reading the latest RV.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes Init() ordering: it now calls `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()` (moved below in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`), whereas previously the watcher was started first. The finding’s concern about an untested order change and a potential event gap between index build and watcher startup is specific and grounded in this diff, but the diff alone doesn’t prove a concrete correctness defect without seeing how `initWatcher()`/event consumption handles missed events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:190 — Now that bleve builds run truly in parallel, the errgroup workers write the shared `err` and totalBatchesIndexed without synchronization, and no -race test covers multi-namespace init.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make bleve index builds more parallel by removing the coarse `cacheMu` lock around `BuildIndex` (now only locking when writing `b.cache[key]`). However, the finding’s specific claim about `pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:190`—errgroup workers concurrently writing a shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` without synchronization—is not verifiable from the provided diff hunks. The shown changes in `search.go` around `init` are limited to capturing `ctx` from `tracer.Start`, swapping logging to `s.log`, and adding an info log; no `errgroup` worker code or shared variables are shown here.
